description.narrative: Support for the Office of the UN Resident Coordinator, RCO, in Colombia. The UN has an extensive presence in the country. Coordination and cooperation, internally and externally, is important but demanding and a strong RCO is crucial for the UN's continued role in Colombia. The contribution therefore aims to strengthen the RCO, in line with the UN reform, and thereby to strengthen the UNsystems' role in peacebuilding in Colombia, through increased capacity for joint analysis, planning, information management and communication. Sida supports two strategic positions at the RCO in Colombia, of which one is Swedish and one is local, and also contributes funding to rapid strategic and catalytic activities of importance for the implementation of the peace agreement between the government and the FARC, as well as the conditions for a complete peace.

Stöd till kontoret för FN-systemets gemensamma land-koordinator, UN Resident Coordinator’s Office (RCO), i Colombia. FN har en omfattande närvaro i landet. Samordning och samarbete, internt och externt, är viktigt men krävande och ett starkt RCO är avgörande för FN:s fortsatta roll i Colombia. Insatsen ämnar därför stärka RCO, i linje med FN-reformen, och därigenom FN:s roll i fredsbyggandet i Colombia, genom ökad kapacitet för gemensam analys, planering, informationshantering och kommunikation. Sida stödjer två strategiska positioner vid RCO i Colombia, varav en svensk och en lokalanställd, och bidrar även med finansiering till snabba strategiska och katalytiska aktiviteter av vikt för genomförandet av fredsavtalet mellan regeringen och FARC, samt förutsättningarna för en fullständig fred.

description.narrative:
The contribution can be categorized into two main results or Outputs.
The first one is to strengthen the capacity of the UN Resident Coordinators Office in Colombia through additional staffmembers within the Office: One P5 level Head of Office and one G6level Associate Officer, with responsibility for the administration of the Swedish contribution. The Swedish funding for the Head of the RCs Office was during the period phased out, and the UN now carries it with central funds, which speaks both to the benefits and continued relevance of the position as well as to the sustainability of the efforts to continue strengthening the RCO in Colombia in line with the ongoing UN reformprocess. The progress on all indicators for Output 1 are significant and Sida concludes that this aspect of the intervention has significantly contributed to strengthening the RCOs capacity.
The second is to strengthen its capacity to lead and coordinate the UNsystem in Colombia by engaging the UN in strategic and catalytic activities for peace building and sustainable development. Under the second Output of the contribution, a total of 17 strategic initiatives were supported by the RCO during the period, ranging from support to local peace building initiatives by Colombian civil society organizations to support for the national governments office for coordination of the Covid19 response, to improved information management within the UNsystem. Sida assesses the initiatives to be strategic and relevant, and the results to be satisfactory
